svg.title: Figure 4. Why crosshead travel overstates strain
svg.desc: Left: schematic of two springs in series between a fixed base and the moving crosshead. The lower spring represents the frame, grips and specimen shoulders with compliance C m; the upper spring represents the specimen reduced section with compliance L c over E A0. Both carry the same load P, and the crosshead travel Delta is the sum of their stretches. Right: engineering stress up to 280 MPa versus strain up to 0.6 percent for an illustrative steel. The extensometer curve rises steeply with slope E; the crosshead-based curve starts with a curved toe from grip seating and then rises with a much smaller slope E app, given by 1 over E app equals 1 over E plus A0 C m over L c.
